release.content: pubkit 0.22.0 was released on 2026-10-30 from commit 63cbf733a0d80d6f79d649cdb003059626f0d699 with these changes.

rows: pubkit protect manages a repository's "Allow auto-merge" setting: "auto_merge": true in its pubkit.json protect block or its protected.json entry turns it on (false turns it off, and without it the setting is left alone), so a pull request can be set to merge by itself once the ruleset's checks pass; --check reports a setting that differs. schryer/visit-ee's entry turns it on
A service's CI tests job keeps pip's and uv's download caches between runs, keyed on the repository's lock files, so its setup installs from the runner instead of PyPI
actions/docker-build builds a Docker image with buildx and a GitHub Actions layer cache, one scope per image, and loads it into the runner's Docker

A pubkit.json protect block or protected.json entry takes "release_app": a GitHub App id, a positive integer, which its release tag ruleset lets through; a repository of the one owner pubkit still knows gets that owner's app when it names none, with a warning. pubkit sync --check now refuses an unsound protect block too

ci.tools in pubkit.json lists what a Rust repository's functional suite drives, each a crate, a git repository and a tag: sync writes it into the functional job, which installs each with cargo install --locked, and the nightly moves each tag to the latest release of its repository. The pub-version input still works, warns at sync, and goes in a later release. pubkit now installs pub from Sustenaut/publet, where it moved

pubkit.json takes "nightly": {"pins": {"crates": [...]}}: the crates the nightly moves with the pins rather than one at a time. pubkit sync --check refuses any other key there, naming it. A repository that names none keeps the old three crates, and `pubkit pins` warns when that moved any of them

pubkit new takes --owner, by default the owner the origin remote names, and without either it stops; a new package's Cargo.toml and SECURITY.md name that owner. It no longer prints lines to add to pubkit's own lists: it prints the protect block to add, and that the repository is then switched on in the release app
Neutral examples replace the names of consumers in the docs, docstrings, error text and test fixtures, and a test fails if what pubkit ships names any repository but its own and its tools'
